title: A scheme finite over a field is affine, the spectrum of a finite-dimensional algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a morphism $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] which is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Make $B=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ a $k$-algebra through the ring map $k=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ induced by $t$. Then $T$ is affine, the canonical morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ (corresponding to the identity of $B=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$) is an isomorphism of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $B$ is finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space.

source.place: Morphisms, Section 03J3 (section-universally-bounded), the paragraph before Definition Tag 03J4, lines 15292-15299 ('If X is finite over k, then X = Spec(A) where A is a finite k-algebra'); it unfolds Morphisms, Definition Tag 01WH (definition-integral, lines 10957-10969: finite = affine, and R -> A finite for every affine open Spec R of the target with inverse image Spec A), applied to the one affine open Spec k of Spec k
